title: Memory spiral under high concurrency causing intermittent OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — runtime micro-repair and customer mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers experienced repeated GPU OOMs and elevated tail latency during sustained multi-tenant bursts on hosted API and Dedicated pools; two Private installs reported KV handle growth and fragmentation leading to degraded throughput.
description: Summary: During a high-concurrency traffic spike last week we observed a progressive memory growth pattern ("memory spiral") across the serving runtime: small per-session KV allocations were not reclaimed quickly, compaction didn't keep pace with allocation patterns, and GPU-side arenas fragmented under mixed sequence lengths. The effect manifests as intermittent OOMs on Hosted, throughput drops on Dedicated pools, and long-tail retries for Private customers. This ticket drives a targeted micro-repair (runtime patch + safer fallback policy) and a customer mitigation playbook for immediate relief.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy the 1k-concurrent clients load generator against a multi-tenant hosted endpoint with mixed short/long sequences; 2) Run a persistent KV-heavy workload that churns session-level metadata and triggers prefix caching; 3) Observe GPU memory usage and process RSS over 30-90 minutes; 4) Verify KV handle count on nodes and check slab/free-list metrics.
root_cause: Combination of three factors: (a) a KV handle retention bug in the session cache where ephemeral handles were retained until GC sweep windows (regression introduced by earlier batching optimization), (b) allocator slab sizing that favored large contiguous blocks causing fragmentation when many small allocations were short-lived, and (c) kernel selection path that kept large activation buffers pinned on GPUs for longer-than-necessary for mixed-sequence workloads.
immediate_mitigations: Push temporary runtime flag to aggressively shrink KV session retention window (runtime toggle: kv.session_retention_ms=30000)
Enable per-node anti-thrashing backpressure: reject new conversational sessions when free-slab ratio < 12%
Roll out model-routing fallback to smaller-activation variants for affected customers (policy-level route)
Coordinate Dedicated pool capacity increase for impacted customers while fixes roll out
Provide Private customers a one-line config to enable session-hint expiration and a hotfix bundle
long_term_fixes: Fix KV handle lifecycle: ensure session-level handles are reference-counted and unlinked deterministically when session idle observed
Allocator rework: adaptive slab allocator to split large slabs for high small-allocation workloads
GPU buffer lifetime optimization: release activation buffers immediately after synchronous dispatch when safe
Introduce periodic in-place compaction task with low-priority throttling to reclaim fragmented slabs without impacting SLOs
Add regression tests that simulate mixed-sequence, high-concurrency workloads and assert no steady-state growth
